findings.title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called with no arguments but only the UserModel-taking overload is defined
findings.body: Line 47 reads `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) {`. The only definition added by this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm.java line 160. There is no no-arg version defined anywhere in the class hierarchy (UsernameForm extends UsernamePasswordForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator). The call therefore does not resolve and the module will not compile. The intended logic was likely `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, mirroring the other call sites in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (line 115) and UsernamePasswordForm.challenge (line 137), which both pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: IS_USER_IDENTIFIED attribute now depends on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators instead of user != null
findings.body: Previously, `isUserIdentified` was set to true whenever `context.getUser() != null`. The refactor moved the assignment inside `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)) { ... isUserIdentified = true; ... }`. WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to always return false (added in this PR), so IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is always sent as "false" to the form template, including re-authentication scenarios where the user IS identified and a UsernameForm or UsernamePasswordForm authenticator has already hidden the username via USERNAME_HIDDEN. Any template logic that switches on IS_USER_IDENTIFIED (e.g., to label the page, scope the listed passkeys, or render a 're-authenticate as X' state) will behave as if no user is identified. A cleaner fix is to compute `boolean isUserIdentified = user != null;` once and keep the authenticator-list gating inside the if-block, so the two concerns are not coupled.

findings.title: try/assertThat/fail/catch pattern is misleading and contains dead `fail()` call
Unused import NoSuchElementException after Assert.assertThrows calls were replaced
findings.body: The diff replaces the two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` assertions with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), Matchers.notNullValue())`, but the import `import org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException;` at line 51 was left behind. NoSuchElementException is no longer referenced anywhere in the file; remove the import.
